full_judgment:
4. Plaintiffs claim that land measuring 17.72 acres appeartaining to khatian No. I corresponding to plot No. 8165 of Mouaza Rameshwarpur under P.S. Gabtali, District Bogra, are the khas land of the Government which has been recorded in the khatian No. 1, the said land which is under the possession of the Government is being used by the people of the locality as a beel/pond for catching fishes and for irrigation. This beet land gradually silted up and became cultivable. During the recent survey the said land is recorded in the name of the Deputy Commissioner, Borga. Plaintiffs-petitioners in number 18 (Eighteen) claimed 8.46 acres out of 17.72 acres by way of pattan on different dates by different lease deeds duly executed and registered in favour of plaintiff-petitioners as of landless people by the defendant No. 1 and as such the alleged claim of the opposite party No. 6 in respect of the development project is absolutely baseless and false. The plaintiff-petitioners have been possessing and enjoying the land settling in their favour by demarcating plots by the respective authorities and the alleged claim of the opposite party No. 6 is baseless. Petitioners further claim that they are enjoying the disputed land peaceful by growing paddy and other crops, which is the only means of their livelihood. 

 7. The defendant-appellant-opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 contested the petition by filing a written objection denying all allegations of the petitioners and conteded inter alia, that the land measuring 17.72 acres appertaining to plot No. 8165 of Mouza Rameshwarpur P.S. Gabtoli, Bogra are the khas land of the Government recorded in Khatian No. 1. The said land which is under the possession of the Government is being used by local people as a beel/pond for catching fishes and using water for irrigation. The further case of the defendants is that the northern side there is a adarshagram on the east-west side of the said adarshagram there are ponds. That during the recent survey the suit land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 D.C. Bogra. That the Govt. allotted 150 metric tons of wheat for an asrayan scheme of Rameshwarpur and as such on 13.2.2000 the Deputy Commissioner, Bogra has directed the Thana Nirbahi Officer to undertake the measure in respect to withdrew the wheat and complete the work within time and as a result 2.94 acres of land has been taken under the asrayan prokalpa. Defendant opposite parties further stated that the plaintiffs are not poor and landless and according to law they are not entitled to get lease of the suit land (being beel). 

 15. The learned Advocate Mr. Mazibar Rahman appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned Additional District Judge allowing the application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendant appellant-opposite party. No.1-4 and 6 staying the operation of the order of status quo passed on 17.4.2000 by the learned Subordinate Judge has committed irregularity find illegality. According to him the Omitted fact that the petitioners are the bonafide lease-holders by registered lease deeds executed by the defendant opposite party No. 1 after observing all formalities thereof and there is no prove to show that the said registered lease deeds have been cancelled by the defendant opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 is absurd. He has further argued that the object of the Government was to rehabilitate the destitute or shelter less or landless is the asrayan prokalpa taken by the Government and the plaintiff-petitioners have got the lease of the khas land of the Government as landless and that the state policy was to rehabiliate the landless people and as such the learned Additional District Judge while disposing the application of opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 did not apply his judicial mind and he was biased. Learned Advocate further submits that the learned Additional District Judge acted illegally in holding that the defendant opposite party Nos. 1-4 and 6 are in possession of the suit land and that the learned Subordinate Judge was justified by granting status quo in respect of the suit land but the learned Additional District Judge acted illegally in total misconception and as such the judgment and order is liable to set aside. 

 16. The learned Advocate Mr. Abul Hossain Azadi A.A.G. appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite parties submits that land measuring 17.72 acres appertaining to Plot No. 8165 of Mouza Rameshwarpur under P.S. Gabtali was the khas land of the Govt. recorded in Khatian No. 1. That the said land under the possession of the Government and local people have been using the same as beel/pond by catching fishes and using water for irrigation. On the north there is an adrashagram and on the east-west of the said adarsha gram there are ponds and during survey the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 (Govt.). Out of total land 2.94 acres of land has been taken under a development programme namely 'Asrayan prokalpa'. The suit land had never been recorded in the name of the plaintiff petitioners. He has further submitted that as per circular dated 10.2.2600 issued by the Project Director, Asrayan Prokalpa Bastabayan Sangstha of the Prime Minister's office 150 metric tons of wheat was sanctioned for earth filling in the suit land. The Deputy Commissioner, Bogra by letter dated 13.2.2000 directed the Thana Nirbahi Officer to do the needful for 'completion of the work in order to provide shelterless and destitute persons. According to him the trial Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the case has granted status quo in respect of the suit land where the Government has under taken a Development scheme for providing shelter and other facilities for the poor and destitute persons. Learned Advocate further pointed out that there was local investigation and from the report of the local investigation it appeared that there exists no paddy field and already 75% work of the Asrayan Prokalpa' had been completed in the suit land. The learned Subordinate Judge in spite of this position granted the order of status quo in respect of the suit land. He has also argued that the learned Subordinate Judge without considering that there exists no legal right of the plaintiff-petitioners and balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in favour of the plaintiff-petitioners granted the order of status quo and that the suit land was khas land since the time of erstwhile East Pakistan and even as per the latest R.O.R. has been recorded in the name of the Govt. The suit land has been marked for development scheme and no order of status quo can be granted in view of the provision of Act No. 32 of 1999. Learned Advocate further submits that the learned lower appellant Court in its judgment held that though the plaintiffs claiming pattan of 8.76 acres of land but they could not show the pattan of the land with any specification. The Advocate Commissioner's report shows there is a adarshagram in the southern side and also a pond in the visinity of the village. According to him the plaintiff-petitioners had already been dispossessed from the suit land and as such the plaintiff-petitioners ought to have prayed for mandatory injunction and cannot seek for an order of status quo. In the instant case there is no clear and specific terms and as such the plaintiff- petitioners cannot claim an order of injunction and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 19. Admittedly, the suit land measuring 8.46 acres out of 17.72 acres appertaining to khatian No 1 of Mouza Rameshwarpur under P.S. Gabtali, District-Bogra corresponding to plot No. 8165 as has been described in the schedule of the plaint was the khas land of the Government and recorded in the name of the Government in Khatian No. 1. It is also not denied that the total land of the plot is a beet (Jalmahal) which gradually silted up and became cultivable. The plaintiff-respondent-petitioners claim that they took lease 8.46 acres of land from the defendant No. I duly executing registered kabuliyats on different dates and by taking lease they also mutated their names and paid rents to the Government and since pattan they have been possessing the said land for more than 12 years. The learned Subordinate Judge while considering the case of both sides came to a conclusion that plaintiffs-respondent-petitioners took settlement of 8.46 acres of land out of plot No. 8165 by way of different registered kabuliyats from the defendant No. 1 and the term embodied in the registered kabuliyats expired and as such title to the land accrued in favour of the petitioners. We have also gone through some certified copies of said registered kabuliyats produced in Court where from we find that as many as 18 persons were granted lease on different dates and those persons executed kabuliyats in favour of defendant No. 1 with respect to their allotted piece of land of which original deeds are said to have been lost and the terms were also different. Someone was granted lease for 99 years, some for 10 years and some for 15 years. From these deeds prima-facie it will appear that they may have lease hold-rights in the suit lands, but no absolute right, title and interest has yet accrued in their favour and the suit as was framed at the stage, claiming declaration of title is not at all maintainable in law and the findings of the learned Subordinate Judge that absolute title to the suit land accrued in their favour is not at all correct. It is the settled principle of law that an incomplete suit should be laid at rest at the earliest moment so that no further time is wasted over what is bound to collapse as not being permitted by law. It further appears from the report of the Advocate Commissioner that there is a adarshagram in the southern side of the suit land and also a pond in the visinity of the village and according to the learned Advocate Commissioner the pond was dug recently by demolishing paddy and other crops grown by the petitioners. Relying on the commissioner's report, learned Additional District Judge came to conclusion that since the petitioners were dispossessed and the defendant No. 1-4 and 6 already took over possession into the suit land, dug pond with pucca stairs and the possession of the defendants into the suit land even if illegal prohibitory injunction cannot be granted without ousting them (defendants) from the suit land. Learned Additional District Judge also opined that the petitioners had to pray for mandatory injunction and as such the learned Additional district Judge allowed the miscellaneous appeal and stayed the operation of the order of status quo.
